question: Prafulla Chaki and Khudiram Bose are known for their attempt to assassinate which British official?​ (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Lord Curzon
Lord Minto
John Morley
Douglas Kingsford
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Douglas Kingsford

Explanation:
Prafulla Chaki and Khudiram Bose were revolutionaries in the Indian independence movement. In 1908, they attempted to assassinate Douglas Kingsford, the British magistrate of Muzaffarpur. Kingsford was known for his harsh actions against anti-partition activists. However, the bomb was mistakenly thrown at a carriage carrying two European women instead of Kingsford, killing them. Khudiram Bose was arrested and hanged, while Prafulla Chaki committed suicide to avoid capture. This incident intensified revolutionary activities against British rule in Bengal. The Muzaffarpur conspiracy highlighted the growing discontent and radicalism among the youth.

☛ When was Khudiram Bose hanged? → 11 August 1908
☛ How old was Khudiram Bose at the time of his execution? → 18 years
☛ Where did Prafulla Chaki commit suicide? → Mokama Railway Station (Bihar)
☛ What was Kingsford's official position? → Magistrate of Muzaffarpur
question_hi: प्रफुल्ल चाकी और खुदीराम बोस को किस ब्रिटिश अधिकारी की हत्या के प्रयास के लिए जाना जाता है? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 3)

लॉर्ड मिंटो
जॉन मॉर्ले
डगलस किंग्सफोर्ड
solution_hi:

Explanation:

question: What was the name of the headquarters of the Ghadar Party? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: Bharat Ashram
Hindustan Ashram
Yugantar Ashram
Azad Ashram
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Yugantar Ashram

Explanation:
The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco, USA. Its headquarters was called Yugantar Ashram. This ashram served as a hub for Indian immigrants and revolutionaries, where the newspaper Ghadar was published. The party aimed to overthrow British rule in India through armed revolution. Key leaders included Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Kartar Singh Sarabha. The movement inspired many Indians abroad to join the freedom struggle.

question:
Which of the following is/are correct about Tej Bahadur Sapru?
I. He helped Annie Besant to build up the Central Hindu College at Banaras.
II. He entered politics during the Home Rule movement.
III. He participated in the Round Table Conferences held between 1930 and 1932 in London. (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Only I
Only II
All I, II and III
Only II and III
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is All I, II and III

Explanation:
Tej Bahadur Sapru was a prominent Indian lawyer, politician, and liberal leader. He helped Annie Besant establish the Central Hindu College at Banaras (later Banaras Hindu University). He entered politics during the Home Rule movement (1916) and emerged as a leader of Indian liberals. Sapru participated in all three Round Table Conferences held in London between 1930 and 1932 as an Indian delegate. He advocated constitutional reforms and communal harmony. Therefore, all three statements are correct.

☛ When did Sapru enter politics? → During the Home Rule movement
☛ Where were the Round Table Conferences held? → London
☛ In which years were the Round Table Conferences held? → 1930, 1931, and 1932
☛ Which ideology did Sapru follow? → Liberalism

question: The Indian Home Rule League at Madras was founded by ______. (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Subhas Chandra Bose
Annie Besant
Mahatma Gandhi
Bala Gangadhar Tilak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Annie Besant

Explanation:
Annie Besant founded the Indian Home Rule League at Madras (now Chennai) in September 1916. Its aim was to secure self-government (Home Rule) for India within the British Empire. Bal Gangadhar Tilak had started a separate Home Rule League in Maharashtra in April 1916. Both leagues worked through public meetings, propaganda, and petitions to energize the independence movement. Annie Besant was a prominent social reformer and later became the president of the Indian National Congress.

☛ Home Rule League founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak → April 1916 in Maharashtra
☛ Home Rule League founded by Annie Besant → September 1916 in Madras
☛ Main objective of Home Rule Movement → To achieve self-government (Dominion Status) within the British Empire
☛ Annie Besant's first achievement → Became president of Indian National Congress in 1917
☛ Propaganda media of Home Rule Leagues → Newspaper 'New India' (Annie Besant) and 'Maratha' (Tilak)

question: Which individuals actively supported Mahatma Gandhi during the Kheda Satyagraha movement? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: Ambalal Sarabhai and Anasuya Ben
Raj Kumar Shukla and Rajendra Prasad
Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yajnik
Vallabhbhai Patel and Rajendra Prasad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yajnik

Explanation:
The 1918 Kheda Satyagraha was a peasant movement in Gujarat for revenue remission. Led by Mahatma Gandhi, it was actively supported by Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yajnik. Patel organized the peasants while Yajnik mobilized public opinion. The movement strengthened Gandhi and Patel's political careers.

question: ______ was Mahatma Gandhi's first successful satyagraha in India.A. KhedaB. BardoliC. ChamparanD. Salt march (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: A
B
D
C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Champaran

Explanation:
Mahatma Gandhi's first successful satyagraha in India was the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917. It was launched in the Champaran district of Bihar against the exploitation of indigo farmers by British planters under the Tinkathia system, which forced farmers to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land. The protest led to the abolition of the oppressive system and marked the beginning of non-violent resistance in India's freedom struggle. This success established Gandhi's leadership and the effectiveness of satyagraha as a tool for social and political change.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Gandhi's first satyagraha in India → Champaran (1917)
☛ Main cause of Champaran Satyagraha → Tinkathia system of indigo cultivation
☛ Kheda Satyagraha → 1918, against tax hike
☛ Bardoli Satyagraha → 1928, led by Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Salt March → 1930, part of Civil Disobedience Movement

question: Which of the following does NOT match? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Swaraj Dal- CR Das
Ved Samaj- Gharalu Naidu
Scientific Society- Syed Ahmed Khan
Bhoodan movement- Vinoba Bhave
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ved Samaj- Gharalu Naidu

Explanation:
Ved Samaj was founded in 1864 by K. Sridharalu Naidu in Chennai, not by Gharalu Naidu. The society was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and emphasized rational religion and social reforms. Gharalu Naidu was a political leader. Other options are correctly matched: Swaraj Dal was founded in 1923 by Motilal Nehru and C. R. Das; Scientific Society was founded in 1864 by Syed Ahmed Khan in Aligarh; Bhoodan movement was started in 1951 by Vinoba Bhave.

question: Which policy of Lord Dalhousie was a significant political cause of the 1857 Revolt? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Dual Government
Doctrine of Lapse
Vernacular Press Act
Ryotwari System
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Doctrine of Lapse

Explanation:
Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse was a major political cause of the 1857 Revolt. Under this policy, if a ruler of a princely state had no natural heir, the state was annexed into the British Empire. This led to the annexation of several states like Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara, etc., causing widespread discontent among Indian rulers and the public. The policy dismantled the traditional ruling system and left many rulers unemployed. Dual Government is associated with Robert Clive, the Vernacular Press Act with Lord Lytton, and the Ryotwari System with Munro. Thus, among political causes, the Doctrine of Lapse was the most significant trigger for the revolt.

question: Why was the Ghadar Party’s revolutionary attempt during World War I largely unsuccessful? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Lack of support from international allies
Strong opposition from the Indian National Congress
Public apathy towards armed revolution
Interception by British intelligence and internal betrayal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public apathy towards armed revolution

Explanation:
The Ghadar Party's revolutionary attempt during World War I was largely unsuccessful because the Indian public was apathetic towards armed revolution. The Ghadar Party had organized overseas Indians, especially in the United States and Canada, to launch a revolt against British rule. However, when the revolutionaries returned to India under the Ghadar Conspiracy of 1915, they did not receive the expected support from the masses. Most Indians remained loyal to the British and cooperated with the war effort. Additionally, revolutionary activities were mostly confined to Bengal, and other regions lacked political awareness. This public apathy prevented the party from staging a large-scale uprising, while the British government carried out severe repression. Thus, public indifference was the primary reason for its failure.

question: In which year was Bal Gangadhar Tilak arrested by the British authorities for writing a seditious article in the newspaper ‘Kesari’? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)

question: What was the immediate cause that sparked the 1857 uprising among Indian sepoys? (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The immediate cause of the 1857 uprising was the use of greased cartridges in Enfield rifles. Soldiers had to bite off the cartridge end before loading, and a rumor spread that the grease used was made from cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim religious sentiments. At Meerut, 85 sepoys refused to use the cartridges, were court-martialed, and given harsh punishment. This spark led to the revolt on May 10, 1857. Other options like heavy taxation and disbandment of local rulers were long-term causes, but the greased cartridges were the immediate trigger.

question: Which of the following freedom fighters led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Jyotirao Phule

solution:

Explanation:
The Mahad Satyagraha was led by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar on 20 March 1927 in Mahad, Maharashtra. The protest aimed to secure the right of Dalits (then called untouchables) to use public water sources, specifically the Chawdar Tank. Ambedkar mobilized about 2,500 followers and marched to the tank, where they drank water, challenging the social discrimination based on caste. This event became a landmark in the Dalit movement for social equality. Later in 1927, Ambedkar also led the public burning of the Manusmriti, a text that justified caste hierarchy. The Mahad Satyagraha is considered a pivotal moment in India's social reform history, highlighting Ambedkar's role as a champion of Dalit rights and his strategy of non-violent protest.

question: Behramji Merwanji Malabari, a Parsi social reformer, is credited for his efforts with the legislative enactment related to which of the following social evils? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 1)

Explanation:
Behramji Merwanji Malabari was a prominent Parsi social reformer who campaigned against social evils like child marriage and widow remarriage in 19th-century India. His efforts led to the enactment of the Age of Consent Act of 1891, which raised the minimum age of marriage for girls to 12 years. This was a significant legislative step to curb child marriage. Malabari used his journal, 'The Indian Social Reformer', and published books to spread awareness. He is most credited for his work related to child marriage legislation. Other reforms like abolition of sati were championed by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, while female infanticide was addressed by later laws. Thus, Malabari's legacy is strongly tied to the fight against child marriage.

बेहरामजी मेरवानजी मालाबारी एक प्रमुख पारसी समाज सुधारक थे, जिन्होंने 19वीं शताब्दी में बाल विवाह और विधवा पुनर्विवाह जैसी सामाजिक बुराइयों के खिलाफ आवाज उठाई। उनके प्रयासों का परिणाम 1891 का बाल विवाह अधिनियम (Age of Consent Act) था, जिसने लड़कियों के विवाह की न्यूनतम आयु 12 वर्ष निर्धारित की। यह अधिनियम बाल विवाह को रोकने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम था। मालाबारी ने अपने लेखन और सार्वजनिक अभियानों के माध्यम से इस सुधार को बढ़ावा दिया। उन्होंने 'द इंडियन सोशल रिफॉर्मर' नामक पत्रिका निकाली और बाल विवाह तथा विधवा पुनर्विवाह पर पुस्तकें लिखीं। इस प्रकार, उन्हें सबसे अधिक श्रेय बाल विवाह से संबंधित विधायी अधिनियमन के लिए दिया जाता है।

question: Keshab Chandra Sen was a prominent leader of which of the following reform movements in India? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 3)

Ramakrishna Mission
solution:

Explanation:
Keshab Chandra Sen (1838-1884) was a prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828. He incorporated elements from Christianity and other religions into the Brahmo Samaj.

question: The weekly journal Young India was associated with whom among the following? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Mahatma Gandhi
Jawaharlal Nehru
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahatma Gandhi

Explanation:
Young India was an English weekly journal launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919. Gandhi used it as a platform to propagate his ideas of non-cooperation and civil disobedience against British rule. The journal played a key role in spreading nationalist thought and mobilizing masses for the freedom struggle. Gandhi also edited other journals like Harijan (1933), Indian Opinion (in South Africa, 1903), and Navajivan (Gujarati). Young India was instrumental in shaping public opinion during the 1920s and promoting the concept of Swaraj. It was banned several times by the British government due to its anti-establishment content.

question_hi: साप्ताहिक पत्रिका यंग इंडिया निम्नलिखित में से किससे संबंधित थी? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 1)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
यंग इंडिया एक अंग्रेजी साप्ताहिक पत्रिका थी जिसे महात्मा गांधी ने 1919 में शुरू किया था। इसका उपयोग गांधीजी ने असहयोग आंदोलन और सविनय अवज्ञा के विचारों को फैलाने के लिए किया। गांधीजी ने 'हरिजन' (1933), 'इंडियन ओपिनियन' (1903 दक्षिण अफ्रीका में) और 'नवजीवन' (गुजराती) जैसे अन्य पत्र भी निकाले। यंग इंडिया में गांधीजी के लेख राष्ट्रवादी जागरण और स्वराज की अवधारणा को बढ़ावा देने वाले थे। इस पत्रिका ने 1920 के दशक में भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम को आकार देने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।
